# MINOR CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS
Minor capital improvements are defined as projects with costs between $35,000 and $250,000 that add new space or alter the programmed design or function of space or building systems, including related fixed equipment, and utility and site development improvements.

Consistent with legislative directives, projects cannot be submitted for work specifically deleted from major capital projects, or for phasing of projects costing in excess of $250,000.

State-funded projects are normally limited to one project-per building-per year.  However, two unrelated projects in the same building in any given year may be combined if their combined cost is kept below the $250,000 limit.

The Chancellor or his/her designee may authorize fund transfers between approved projects as long as any transfer does not increase a project cost above $250,000.

Chancellors are authorized to approve minor capital improvement projects costing no more than $250,000 that are not included in the State-funded MCI Program.

These projects may not involve substantial program modifications to a project previously approved by The Regents.

Qualifying projects are those projects with costs between $35,000 and $250,000 which are funded from sources such as Federal funds, gift funds, Hospital Reserve funds, Opportunity funds, and Registration Fees.  General funds (19900A) may not be used to fully or partially fund projects costing $35,000 or more.

keenable.title: 7 CFR 1753.80 -- Minor construction procedure.
keenable.snippet:
(a) If the borrower performs minor construction financed with loan funds, the borrower's regular work order procedure shall be used to administer construction activities that may be performed entirely by a contractor under Form 773 contract, by work order, or jointly by work order and one or more contractors under Form 773 contracts.
(b) RUS financing under Form 773 contracts dated in the same calendar year is limited to the following amounts for the following discrete categories of minor construction. The date of the Form 773 contract is the date the Form 773 contract is executed.
(1) For outside plant construction, the limit is $500,000 or ten per cent (10%) of the borrower's previous calendar year's outside plant total construction, whichever is greater.
(2) For central office equipment, the limit is $500,000.
(3) For equipment and buildings, the limit is $250,000 in each category.

(d) RUS approval must be obtained in advance for minor construction unless all of the following conditions are met:
(1) RUS has approved the engineering design.
(2) All standard RUS procedures are followed, including the application of RUS construction practices (see § 1753.6).
(3) The Standard Form 773 contract is used without modification.

(f) The borrower shall maintain accounting and plant records sufficient to document the cost and location of all construction and to support loan fund advances and disbursements.

(h) RUS will advance funds to finance minor construction work projects only if all necessary documents, including an FRS and supporting data covering the project, are received within one year of the date construction of the project is completed.

Russian govt approves list of 24 most important IT projects costing 14.4 bln rubles
  
  
MOSCOW. Aug 11 (Interfax) - The Russian government has approved a list of "particularly important projects" aimed at substituting imported software for the development of the digital economy, the Russian Digital Development Ministry said in a statement.
The program for selecting and providing support to such projects was launched in 2022. Customers of software import substitution projects which were selected as "particularly important" will be able to claim 50% of the price as a government grant.
The Digital Development Ministry said that the newly approved list contained 24 projects at an overall cost of 14.4 billion rubles, to be implemented using companies' own funds. For the transport sphere, 12 projects costing 11.66 billion rubles have been approved, as well as eight industry and trade projects costing 2.38 billion rubles, three communications and media projects costing 281.2 million rubles and one project in the agroindustrial and fisheries industry at a cost of 54.1 million rubles.
The ministry also said that projects had been approved for developing control systems for technological processes, design documentation and procurement in industry, as well as an end-to-end industrial analytics platform. Projects selected in the transport industry are aimed at developing solutions for aviation, airports, railway infrastructure and logistics, including ERP systems, digital management platforms and artificial intelligence technology.
In communications and media, the projects selected concern the development of Russian solutions for operating network equipment, infrastructure inventorying and authentication services.

octen.title: Ukraine prepares two low-cost domestic missiles for combat use against jet-powered Geran drones
octen.snippet:
Ukraine prepares two low-cost domestic missiles for combat use against jet-powered Geran drones

Iryna Levytska- 18 October, 12:11

Two Ukrainian teams are preparing domestically developed surface-to-air missiles for combat use against Russian jet-powered drones.

Source: Andrii Hrytseniuk, head of the Ukrainian defence-tech cluster Brave1, in an interview with Ukrainska Pravda

Details:"They are cheap and easy to manufacture. One of the requirements was to keep the cost of a missile below US\$20,000," Hrytseniuk said.

The ambition of these projects is underscored by the average market cost of missiles, ranging from hundreds of thousands of dollars per shot for a Stinger to half a million dollars for an AIM-9X missile used by F-16 fighter jets.

Even using two or three such missiles against a Russian long-range drone is expected to be cost-effective relative to the value of the target. Various estimates put the cost of a standard Geran at around US\$70,000, while its jet-powered version may cost tens of thousands of dollars more.

Hrytseniuk said Brave1 began funding the development of surface-to-air missiles in 2024. It took two years to produce the first prototypes. A total of 10 Ukrainian teams are working on such missiles.

Background: In May, it was reported that Ukraine is developing low-cost interceptor missiles and had already tested some solutions. Then-defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov said there were plans to scale up their production dozens of times.

The policies, procedures and requirements included in this part are intended to implement provisions of the standard form of loan documents between the Rural Utilities Service (RUS) and its electric borrowers. Each borrower is responsible for the planning, design, construction, operation and maintenance of its electric system. seltz.snippet:
(a) If the borrower performs minor construction financed with loan funds, the borrower's regular work order procedure shall be used to administer construction activities that may be performed entirely by a contractor under Form 773 contract, by work order, or jointly by work order and one or more contractors under Form 773 contracts.

(b) RUS financing under Form 773 contracts dated in the same calendar year is limited to the following amounts for the following discrete categories of minor construction. The date of the Form 773 contract is the date the Form 773 contract is executed.

(1) For outside plant construction, the limit is $500,000 or ten per cent (10%) of the borrower's previous calendar year's outside plant total construction, whichever is greater.

(2) For central office equipment, the limit is $500,000.

(3) For equipment and buildings, the limit is $250,000 in each category.

(c) A single minor construction project may be a discrete element of a somewhat larger overall project, such as the provision and installation of a standby power generator or heating/air conditioning equipment in connection with a building modification or expansion project or the splicing on a major cable placement project. It cannot be a portion, by dividing into smaller segments, of a discrete major construction project, such as the placement of a continuous cable facility.

(d) RUS approval must be obtained in advance for minor construction unless all of the following conditions are met:

(1) RUS has approved the engineering design.

(2) All standard RUS procedures are followed, including the application of RUS construction practices (see \§ 1753.6).

(3) The Standard Form 773 contract is used without modification.

(e) The borrower shall determine the scope of each proposed construction project and decide how it will be constructed. A work project number shall be assigned to which all charges for that project are referenced.

ultimate.title: 7 CFR 1753.80 -- Minor construction procedure.
ultimate.snippet:
(a) If the borrower performs minor construction financed with loan funds, the borrower's regular work order procedure shall be used to administer construction activities that may be performed entirely by a contractor under Form 773 contract, by work order, or jointly by work order and one or more contractors under Form 773 contracts.
(b) RUS financing under Form 773 contracts dated in the same calendar year is limited to the following amounts for the following discrete categories of minor construction. The date of the Form 773 contract is the date the Form 773 contract is executed.
(1) For outside plant construction, the limit is $500,000 or ten per cent (10%) of the borrower's previous calendar year's outside plant total construction, whichever is greater.
(2) For central office equipment, the limit is $500,000.
(3) For equipment and buildings, the limit is $250,000 in each category.

(d) RUS approval must be obtained in advance for minor construction unless all of the following conditions are met:
(1) RUS has approved the engineering design.
(2) All standard RUS procedures are followed, including the application of RUS construction practices (see § 1753.6).
(3) The Standard Form 773 contract is used without modification.

(f) The borrower shall maintain accounting and plant records sufficient to document the cost and location of all construction and to support loan fund advances and disbursements.

(h) RUS will advance funds to finance minor construction work projects only if all necessary documents, including an FRS and supporting data covering the project, are received within one year of the date construction of the project is completed.
